name: Executive order of October 29, 1873 making an addition to the Lake Winnibigoshish reservation
nations: Lake Winnibigoshish band of Chippewa (Ojibwe), now within the Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe
promises: An addition, not a cession: the President set apart an addition to the Lake Winnibigoshish reservation established by article 1 of the treaty of March 19, 1867, along the eastern line of the Leech Lake reservation in township 55 north, range 27 west (Royce).

Royce records that the tract was taken from the land ceded to the United States by the first article of the treaty of March 19, 1867, and refers to the executive order of May 26, 1874, which made a second addition.
today: The Leech Lake Band says the Nelson Act of 1889 opened the unallotted reservation land to timber companies, railroads and settlers.

nationVoice.summary: The Band's history says treaties set aside reservations that would forever be home of the Ojibwe, but the Nelson Act of 1889 opened the unallotted land to timber companies, railroads and settlers, and allotments were later lost through tax forfeiture, sales and fraud.

sources.title: Royce, Indian Land Cessions in the United States (18th Annual Report of the Bureau of American Ethnology, 1899), schedule pages 866-867, executive order of October 29, 1873
Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe, History

openQuestions: The order gave land to the bands, so no promise of its own was found to have been broken. The loss came with the Nelson Act agreements of 1889, which have their own queue entries; the Minnesota Chippewa Tribe's Nelson Act claims before the Indian Claims Commission were not reopened here.

treaties.json lists Mille Lacs and White Earth as present-day tribes; the additions were to the Leech Lake and Winnibigoshish reserves, now part of the Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe, which is not listed. Not edited.
The order was read only in Royce's summary, not in Kappler vol. 1.

See cession-1874-05-26-chippewa-of-the-mississippi for the second additions; Royce records that the Pillager and Winnibigoshish bands ceded their reservations under the Nelson Act agreement signed August 21, 1889.

plain.promised: An addition, not a cession. The President added land to the Lake Winnibigoshish reservation, land the Chippewa had ceded in 1867.
plain.happened: No breach of this order was found. The Leech Lake Band says the reservations were later opened to timber companies and settlers under the Nelson Act of 1889.
plain.today: Nothing was paid or returned under this order. The Nelson Act losses have their own records.
